summary: extruct is a Python library from Scrapinghub (the company behind Scrapy) that extracts embedded structured metadata from HTML pages across six syntaxes: W3C Microdata, JSON-LD, Open Graph, Microformat, RDFa, and Dublin Core. At its core, `_extruct.py` dispatches to individual extractor classes — each implementing a uniform `extract_items(document, base_url)` method — that parse the HTML (or accept a pre-parsed lxml tree) and yield lists of dicts keyed by syntax name. The microdata extractor is the most sophisticated, implementing the full W3C Microdata algorithm with itemref traversal, nested items, and property value resolution by element type; JSON-LD is a thin wrapper around `json.loads` plus `jstyleson` for comment-stripping; Open Graph scans `<meta property>` tags; RDFa delegates entirely to the `pyRdfa`/`rdflib` Graph stack; Microformat is a one-line passthrough to `mf2py.parse()`; and Dublin Core maps `<meta name>` and `<link rel>` elements against catalogued DC term URIs. An optional `uniform=True` mode normalizes microdata, microformat, Open Graph, and Dublin Core into flat `{"@context": ..., "@type": ..., ...keys...}` dicts, though RDFa uniforming is explicitly not yet implemented.

findings.description: 1. All-in-one metadata extraction via `extruct.extract()` dispatching across 6 syntaxes with a single string-or-tree interface. 2. W3C Microdata extraction: full algorithm support including nested items (itemscope linking), itemref cross-references, property type resolution (img/src, a/href, meta/content, time/datetime, etc.), and optional htmlText node references. 3. JSON-LD extraction from `<script type="application/ld+json">` blocks with comment-stripping fallback via jnewshead for malformed scripts. 4. Open Graph extraction: scans `<meta property="og:...">` and parses RDFa-style prefix declarations for namespace resolution. 5. RDFa extraction: delegates to `pyRdfa3` + `rdflib` with a custom namespace expansion and a multi-value ordering fix. 6. Microformat extraction: thin wrapper over `mf2py.parse()` with lxml parser backend. 7. Dublin Core extraction: populates elements and terms from `<meta name="DC.xxx">` and `<link rel="DCTERMS.xxx">` using hardcoded URI catalogues. 8. Uniform output mode normalizes microdata/microformat/opengraph/dublincore into `{"@context": ..., "@type": ..., }` but excludes RDFa. 9. CLI tool (`extruct <URL>`) with syntax filtering via `--syntaxes`. 10. Parsed tree reuse: accepts pre-parsed lxml trees to avoid double-parsing in pipelines.

apiSurface: Primary API: `extruct.extract(htmlstring_or_tree, base_url=None, encoding='UTF-8', syntaxes=['microdata','opengraph','json-ld','microformat','rdfa','dublincore'], errors='strict', uniform=False, return_html_node=True, schema_context=' http://schema.org') -> dict[str, list[dict]]`. Returns a dict keyed by syntax name, each value a list of extracted item dicts. Individual extractor classes: `Json Ld Extractor().extract(htmlstring)`, `MicrodataExtractor().extract(htmlstring)`, `OpenGraphExtractor().extract(htmlstring)`, `RDFaExtractor().extract(htmlstring)` (experimental), `MicroformatExtractor().extract(htmlstring)`, `DublinCoreExtractor().extract(htmlstring)`. Each also has `extract_items(tree, item)` for use with pre-parsed trees. CLI: `extruct <url> --syntaxes microdata json-json json-json --json-json json-json --uniform --errors log`. Dependency stack: lxml, rdflib, pyrdfOTFa3, mf2py, w3lib, html-text, jstyleson. Non-CLI users who do not want `requests` pulling in.
integrationPoints: Natural fit for a`Playwright → HTML → extruct → structured data → queue → comparison/merge → DB` pipeline. Accepted play: 1. Use `page.content()` from Playwright as the `htmlstring` input. 2. Parse once with lxml, reuse the tree across all extractors except microformat (pass raw string for that). 3. Focus extraction on `microdata` and `json-ioins` syntaxes since e-commerce product pages are filled with schema.org markup (Product, Offers, Review, BreadcrumbList). 4. Feed the resulting dicts into a JSONB column or normalize into a product table. 5. The `uniform=True` output is consumable directly by a matching algorithm comparing two laptop product pages. The `errors='log'` setting  prevents one broken syntax from killing the entire page to extract. For a queue-based pipeline: wrap this in a Celery or RQ worker that accepts URLs, passes HTML through extruct, and emits structured metadata dicts to downstream matching/g matching/aggregation stages.
strengthsForVeridian: 1. Battle-tested by Scrapy/Scrapinghut — within the web scraping ecosystem, this is the de facto standard for structured metadata extraction. 2. Pure focus on HTML input, no HTTP fetching — decoupled design makes it great for inserting into a pipeline that already holds the HTML (useful PageOOLS). 3. Six-syntax extraction in a single call avoids building separate parsers per metadata format. 4. Accepts pre-parsed lxml trees, optimizing CPU reuse — in a loop, parse HTML once, pass the tree to extract, and 6. The microdata, JSON-LD, and OG extractors have extensive handling for messy real-world markup (comment stripping, jnewshead fallback, non-standard OG prefixes like 'product'). 6. The `uniform` mode makes downstream consumption legible and deterministic, transforming raw extraction output into a normalized format friendly for comparison or per 7. Lightweight and well-understood dependency chain — no ML, no external services, no licensing landmines.
weaknessesForVeridian: 1. Near-zero maintenance velocity: 2 commits in 2025, 4-month gap since last commit. The repo appears to be in semi-maintenance mode. 2. RDFa extraction remains experimental and broken with respect to uniform normalization — explicit exceptions for RDFa in the uniform path. 3. The xmDom parsing path for RDFa adds a slightly baroque lxml→DOM→lxml wrapper layer that could become fragile against lxml version upgrades. 4. microformat extraction blocks pre-parsed rdf3/m; string-only — a minor minor inconvenience but complicates pipeline design. 5. Full dependency weight: `rdflib` is a large dependency for just the RDFa path, and `pyRdfatr` is a small maintained package. If you don't need RDFa, you can skip all of that. 6. No extraction standard beyond the big six — if a site uses Twitter Cards, `<meta itemprop>` variant, or custom meta encoding, there's no extensibility mechanism for custom extractors. 7. No structured schema type mapping — what's a `Product vs. `Offer vs. `NewsArticle` comes out of the raw markup without in-library transformations. You have to do that downstream. 8. Version 0.18.0 suggests functional maturity but institutional confidence not (semver principle) — a release that breaks from C versioning (<1.0) carries sempirical risk.
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
